02 — A place to beginDifferent stories. Your own pace.

What’s asking
for your attention?

There isn’t a perfect way to begin.
Choose a thought to explore how an initial conversation could start.

Start with what feels loudest.

You don’t need to sort everything out before reaching out. An initial conversation can help you describe what’s been taking up space, ask questions, and consider whether working together feels right.

A possible way to start
“I’m not sure where to begin, but I’ve had a lot on my mind.”

There is no script you need to follow. This is simply an example of how a conversation can begin.

Illustrative conversation starters. Areas of practice will be confirmed with the counsellor.

You can take

about working together?

A simple beginning.

A few words are enough.

You can ask about availability and share a little about what you’re looking for. There’s no need to put your whole story in an email.

05 — The practical thingsClear information. Fewer unknowns.

Wondering
about something?

The details matter, too. Here’s where you’ll find the essentials before getting in touch.

Where would we meet?

[Add his verified Vancouver practice address, accessibility information, and whether virtual sessions are available.]

What does a session cost?

[Add confirmed fees, session length, cancellation policy and payment methods.]

Is counselling covered by insurance?

[Add his exact professional designation and receipt details. Clients should confirm coverage directly with their benefits provider.]

How do I know if we’re a good fit?

You’re welcome to ask about his experience and approach before deciding. [Add his actual consultation options and who he works with.]

What happens when I reach out?

[Add the real contact method, expected response time and next steps. This concept does not send or store messages.]
